symbols.symbol: Prophetic phrase: first year of Darius
symbols.meaning: Daniel 11 opens by looking back to the first year of Darius the Mede, about 539/538 B.C., the transition year after Babylon fell. It marks a step in the prophetic sequence rather than introducing a separate coded symbol.

wordNotes.explanation: Daniel 11 opens by looking back to the first year of Darius the Mede, about 539/538 B.C., the transition year after Babylon fell.

The final vision itself was received in the third year of Cyrus in Daniel 10, about 536/535 B.C., but the messenger begins by remembering how he stood to confirm and strengthen Darius at the start of Medo-Persian rule.

notes.crossReferenceNotes: Daniel 8 identifies Medo-Persia and Greece before Daniel 11 expands the same transition in historical sequence.

symbols.meaning: Xerxes, the wealthy Persian ruler who stirred up conflict with Greece.

wordNotes.term: stand up yet three kings in Persia
wordNotes.explanation: After Cyrus, the three Persian kings are Cambyses II, the brief usurper Bardiya or Gaumata often called False Smerdis, and Darius I Hystaspes.
The fourth is Xerxes, who becomes especially rich and stirs up conflict with Greece.

symbols.meaning: A mighty king rises, rules with great dominion, and does according to his will. It marks a step in the prophetic sequence rather than introducing a separate coded symbol.

wordNotes.explanation: A mighty king rises, rules with great dominion, and does according to his will.
The language is brief, but it captures the astonishing career of Alexander the Great, whose Greek armies moved with speed and force after Persia's dominance weakened.

notes.crossReferenceNotes: Daniel 8 and Daniel 11 agree that Greece would not remain united after its first great ruler.

symbols.meaning: The fourfold division of Alexander's empire after his death.

wordNotes.explanation: At the height of Alexander's power, his kingdom is broken and divided toward the four winds of heaven.
At the height of Alexander's power, his kingdom is broken and divided toward the four winds of heaven.

notes.crossReferenceNotes: North and south are first measured from the covenant land, which lay between Syria and Egypt.

symbols.meaning: Egypt under the Ptolemies in the early north-south section of the prophecy.
The Seleucid power centered north of the covenant land before Rome takes the northern role.

wordNotes.explanation: The line opens with the strength of the king of the south, Ptolemy I Soter in Egypt, but it ends with Seleucus I Nicator becoming stronger and holding the greater dominion through the Seleucid kingdom that stretched from Syria deep into the eastern territories.
Daniel now narrows the prophecy from the four Greek divisions to two lines of pressure around the covenant land.

symbols.symbol: Prophetic phrase: king of the north
symbols.meaning: After years of conflict, the southern king Ptolemy II Philadelphus tries to secure peace by giving his daughter Berenice in marriage to Antiochus II Theos, the king of the north. It marks a step in the prophetic sequence rather than introducing a separate coded symbol.

wordNotes.explanation: After years of conflict, the southern king Ptolemy II Philadelphus tries to secure peace by giving his daughter Berenice in marriage to Antiochus II Theos, the king of the north.
The alliance looks diplomatic, but Daniel says it will not retain strength; by the end of the episode the southern plan collapses inside the Seleucid court through betrayal and bloodshed.

symbols.symbol: Prophetic phrase: branch of her roots
symbols.meaning: A branch from Berenice's family line rises after her murder. It marks a step in the prophetic sequence rather than introducing a separate coded symbol.

wordNotes.explanation: A branch from Berenice's family line rises after her murder.
Daniel 11:7 keeps the king of the north language tied to the northern side of the conflict.

symbols.meaning: Ptolemy III's southern campaign carries idols, princes, and precious vessels back into Egypt. It marks a step in the prophetic sequence rather than introducing a separate coded symbol.

wordNotes.explanation: Ptolemy III's southern campaign carries idols, princes, and precious vessels back into Egypt.
Daniel 11:8 keeps the king of the north language tied to the northern side of the conflict.

symbols.symbol: Prophetic phrase: king of the south
symbols.meaning: Daniel 11:9 keeps the king of the south language tied to the southern side of the conflict. It marks a step in the prophetic sequence rather than introducing a separate coded symbol.

wordNotes.explanation: Daniel 11:9 keeps the king of the south language tied to the southern side of the conflict.
The southern king returns to his own land after the campaign.

symbols.symbol: Prophetic phrase: his sons shall be stirred up
symbols.meaning: The sons of the northern king gather great forces and renew the Seleucid advance. It marks a step in the prophetic sequence rather than introducing a separate coded symbol.

wordNotes.term: his sons shall be stirred up
wordNotes.explanation: The sons of the northern king gather great forces and renew the Seleucid advance.
The sons of the northern king gather great forces and renew the Seleucid advance.

symbols.symbol: Prophetic phrase: king of the north
symbols.meaning: The king of the south, Ptolemy IV Philopator, fights the king of the north, Antiochus III, and gains a major victory. It marks a step in the prophetic sequence rather than introducing a separate coded symbol.

wordNotes.explanation: The king of the south, Ptolemy IV Philopator, fights the king of the north, Antiochus III, and gains a major victory.
This fits the Battle of Raphia in 217 B.C., where Egypt checked the Seleucid advance and received a large multitude into its hand.

symbols.meaning: After Ptolemy IV's great victory, his heart is lifted up. It marks a step in the prophetic sequence rather than introducing a separate coded symbol.

wordNotes.explanation: After Ptolemy IV's great victory, his heart is lifted up.
He casts down many, but he is not strengthened by the triumph; the south has the immediate advantage, yet the victory is spiritually and politically hollow.

symbols.symbol: Prophetic phrase: king of the north shall return
symbols.meaning: The king of the north returns after years with a greater multitude and more resources than before. It marks a step in the prophetic sequence rather than introducing a separate coded symbol.

wordNotes.term: king of the north shall return
wordNotes.explanation: The king of the north returns after years with a greater multitude and more resources than before.

wordNotes.term: great army and with much riches
wordNotes.explanation: Antiochus III rebuilds Seleucid strength after Raphia and comes again when Egypt is weakened under the young Ptolemy V Epiphanes.

symbols.meaning: Those who try to establish the vision by self-exalting methods only show that they have not understood the God who gave it. It marks a step in the prophetic sequence rather than introducing a separate coded symbol.

wordNotes.explanation: Those who try to establish the vision by self-exalting methods only show that they have not understood the God who gave it.
Many stand up against the king of the south.

symbols.meaning: The king of the north takes fortified cities, and the arms of the south cannot withstand him. It marks a step in the prophetic sequence rather than introducing a separate coded symbol.

wordNotes.explanation: The king of the north takes fortified cities, and the arms of the south cannot withstand him.
Daniel's north-south section keeps showing how unstable earthly protection can be.

notes.crossReferenceNotes: Rome's entrance into the glorious land prepares the setting for the taxation of Augustus, the rule of Tiberius, and the cross.

symbols.meaning: The covenant land where Rome would stand before the Messiah's appearing and Jerusalem's later destruction.

wordNotes.explanation: He stands in the glorious land, which is consumed by his hand.

wordNotes.term: which by his hand shall be consumed
wordNotes.explanation: A new power comes according to his own will, and none can stand before him.

symbols.meaning: The ruler sets his face to enter with the strength of his whole kingdom and brings an arrangement involving a daughter of women, but the plan does not finally stand for him. It marks a step in the prophetic sequence rather than introducing a separate coded symbol.

wordNotes.explanation: The ruler sets his face to enter with the strength of his whole kingdom and brings an arrangement involving a daughter of women, but the plan does not finally stand for him.
Jewish support under Antipater helped Caesar, which explains the reference to upright ones joining the movement.

symbols.symbol: Prophetic phrase: turn his face unto the isles
symbols.meaning: The ruler turns toward the isles and takes many, but a prince causes the reproach to cease and turns it back on him. It marks a step in the prophetic sequence rather than introducing a separate coded symbol.

wordNotes.term: turn his face unto the isles
wordNotes.explanation: The ruler turns toward the isles and takes many, but a prince causes the reproach to cease and turns it back on him.

wordNotes.term: a prince for his own behalf
wordNotes.explanation: The line fits Julius Caesar's campaigns beyond the eastern Mediterranean world and the eventual check placed upon his course.

symbols.symbol: Prophetic phrase: fort of his own land
symbols.meaning: The ruler turns toward the fort of his own land, but he stumbles, falls, and is not found. It marks a step in the prophetic sequence rather than introducing a separate coded symbol.

wordNotes.explanation: The ruler turns toward the fort of his own land, but he stumbles, falls, and is not found.
The empire-building energy that conquered abroad could not secure peace within its own political heart.

symbols.meaning: Another ruler stands up as a raiser of taxes in the glory of the kingdom, but he is destroyed neither in anger nor in battle. It marks a step in the prophetic sequence rather than introducing a separate coded symbol.

wordNotes.explanation: Another ruler stands up as a raiser of taxes in the glory of the kingdom, but he is destroyed neither in anger nor in battle.
Luke 2 places the birth of Christ in the setting of a decree from Caesar Augustus that all the world should be taxed.

symbols.meaning: A vile person stands up without the honor of the kingdom, yet he comes in peaceably and obtains the kingdom by flatteries. It marks a step in the prophetic sequence rather than introducing a separate coded symbol.

wordNotes.explanation: A vile person stands up without the honor of the kingdom, yet he comes in peaceably and obtains the kingdom by flatteries.
A vile person stands up without the honor of the kingdom, yet he comes in peaceably and obtains the kingdom by flatteries.

notes.crossReferenceNotes: The cutting off of Messiah marks the covenant center of the passage and explains why later language expands from local Israel to the worldwide people of Christ.

symbols.meaning: Christ, cut off under Roman authority as Daniel 9 foretold.

wordNotes.explanation: The arms of a flood are swept away, and the Prince of the covenant is broken.
The arms of a flood are swept away, and the Prince of the covenant is broken.

notes.crossReferenceNotes: Daniel 7, Daniel 8, Daniel 11, and Paul describe the same broad movement from Roman power toward religious self-exaltation.

symbols.meaning: The rise of religious-political compromise through alliance rather than open conquest.

wordNotes.term: after the league made with him
wordNotes.explanation: After a league is made, the power works deceitfully and becomes strong with a small people.
After a league is made, the power works deceitfully and becomes strong with a small people.

notes.crossReferenceNotes: The transition section should be read with Daniel 7, Daniel 8, and Daniel 12 because all three address the rise and activity of the same later power.

symbols.meaning: A prophetic period connected with the rise of the compromised religious-political power.

wordNotes.explanation: The power enters peaceably into rich places, scatters spoil, and devises plans for a time.
The action is not described as a sudden battlefield victory but as a strategic spread of influence.

notes.crossReferenceNotes: Verses 24-31 include a careful transition where interpreters differ on timing, but the movement reaches the same church-state abomination.

symbols.meaning: The king of the north increasingly points to papal Rome, while the south takes on the character of pagan resistance.

wordNotes.explanation: The king of the north stirs up power and courage against the king of the south with a great army, while the king of the south responds with a very great and mighty army but does not stand.
The king of the north stirs up power and courage against the king of the south with a great army, while the king of the south responds with a very great and mighty army but does not stand.

symbols.symbol: Prophetic phrase: they that feed of the portion of his meat
symbols.meaning: Those who eat the king's meat destroy him, his army overflows, and many fall slain. It marks a step in the prophetic sequence rather than introducing a separate coded symbol.

wordNotes.term: they that feed of the portion of his meat
wordNotes.explanation: Those who eat the king's meat destroy him, his army overflows, and many fall slain.
In the transition reading, this fits the collapse of pagan resistance from within.

symbols.symbol: Prophetic phrase: both these kings hearts
symbols.meaning: Both kings sit at one table with hearts set on mischief, speaking lies, but the matter does not prosper because the end is still for the appointed time. It marks a step in the prophetic sequence rather than introducing a separate coded symbol.

wordNotes.explanation: Both kings sit at one table with hearts set on mischief, speaking lies, but the matter does not prosper because the end is still for the appointed time.
A treaty table can sound peaceful while the heart remains set on mischief.

notes.crossReferenceNotes: The covenant issue is worship under Christ's authority, not worship reshaped by civil power.

symbols.meaning: God's authority over worship, conscience, and covenant loyalty.

wordNotes.explanation: The ruler returns with great riches, and his heart is against the holy covenant.
The ruler returns with great riches, and his heart is against the holy covenant.

symbols.meaning: At the appointed time the power returns toward the south, but this movement is not like the former or the latter. It marks a step in the prophetic sequence rather than introducing a separate coded symbol.

wordNotes.explanation: At the appointed time the power returns toward the south, but this movement is not like the former or the latter.

wordNotes.term: return and come toward the south
wordNotes.explanation: The movement toward the south is part of the broader struggle by which pagan political resistance gave way before the Christianized imperial order.

symbols.meaning: Ships of Chittim come against him; he is grieved, returns, and has indignation against the holy covenant. It marks a step in the prophetic sequence rather than introducing a separate coded symbol.

wordNotes.explanation: Ships of Chittim come against him; he is grieved, returns, and has indignation against the holy covenant.
The phrase 'have intelligence with them that forsake the holy covenant' is sobering.

notes.crossReferenceNotes: Daniel 12:11 links the removal of the daily and the setting up of the abomination with the 1290 years, while Daniel 7 and Revelation 13 give the related 1260-year supremacy.

symbols.meaning: The continual pagan system displaced as papal Rome rises, while Christ's true heavenly ministry is also obscured by the papal phase.
Religious authority joined to civil force in opposition to Christ's truth and His people.

wordNotes.explanation: Arms stand on his part, the sanctuary of strength is polluted, the daily is taken away, and the abomination that maketh desolate is placed.
Still, the sanctuary issue remains Christ-centered because the papal phase obscures the truth of Christ's heavenly ministry through counterfeit priesthood, mediation, sacrifice, and tradition.

notes.crossReferenceNotes: Daniel's earlier stories show the same kind of covenant loyalty that prophecy later describes.

symbols.meaning: Faithful witnesses strengthened by personal knowledge of God under religious pressure.

wordNotes.explanation: Those who do wickedly against the covenant are corrupted by flatteries, but the people who know their God are strong and do exploits.
Yet God preserved witnesses who knew Him personally and therefore could not be bought by advantage.

symbols.symbol: Prophetic phrase: they that understand among the people
symbols.meaning: Those who understand among the people instruct many, yet they suffer by sword, flame, captivity, and spoil for many days. It marks a step in the prophetic sequence rather than introducing a separate coded symbol.

wordNotes.term: they that understand among the people
wordNotes.explanation: Those who understand among the people instruct many, yet they suffer by sword, flame, captivity, and spoil for many days.
The little horn uses pressure and persecution; God's people instruct, endure, and bear witness.

symbols.meaning: When the faithful fall, they receive a little help, but many join them with flatteries. It marks a step in the prophetic sequence rather than introducing a separate coded symbol.

wordNotes.explanation: When the faithful fall, they receive a little help, but many join them with flatteries.
Princes, magistrates, translators, preachers, and common believers aided the recovery of Scripture and gospel truth.

notes.crossReferenceNotes: Daniel 12 locates the time of the end after the time, times, and half a time.

symbols.meaning: The period beginning after the 1260 years, marked in prophecy by A.D. 1798.

wordNotes.explanation: Some of those with understanding fall, and the purpose is to try, purge, and make white until the time of the end.

wordNotes.term: to purge, and to make them white
wordNotes.explanation: The time of the end begins after the 1260-year period, reaching its marker in A.D.

notes.crossReferenceNotes: The same self-exalting pattern appears in Daniel, Paul, and Revelation.

symbols.meaning: Papal Rome claiming religious authority above God's Word and against Christ's supremacy.

wordNotes.explanation: The king acts according to his will, exalts himself, magnifies himself above every god, and speaks marvelous things against the God of gods.
Paul uses the same pattern when he describes the man of sin exalting himself in the temple of God.

symbols.symbol: Prophetic phrase: God of his fathers
symbols.meaning: The king disregards the God of his fathers, the desire of women, and every god, because he magnifies himself above all. It marks a step in the prophetic sequence rather than introducing a separate coded symbol.

wordNotes.explanation: The king disregards the God of his fathers, the desire of women, and every god, because he magnifies himself above all.
The desire of women points to the rejection of marriage through enforced celibacy in the priesthood.

symbols.meaning: In his place he honors the god of forces, and a god unknown to his fathers with gold, silver, precious stones, and pleasant things. It marks a step in the prophetic sequence rather than introducing a separate coded symbol.

wordNotes.explanation: In his place he honors the god of forces, and a god unknown to his fathers with gold, silver, precious stones, and pleasant things.

wordNotes.term: god whom his fathers knew not
wordNotes.explanation: The strange god points to forms of devotion and mediation unknown to apostolic Christianity.

symbols.meaning: The king works in strongholds with a strange god, increases glory, causes some to rule over many, and divides land for gain. It marks a step in the prophetic sequence rather than introducing a separate coded symbol.

wordNotes.explanation: The king works in strongholds with a strange god, increases glory, causes some to rule over many, and divides land for gain.
This fits the medieval pattern in which religious authority could distribute honors, influence rulers, sanction conquests, and reward loyalty with land or privilege.

notes.crossReferenceNotes: Revelation 11 uses spiritual Egypt language for anti-biblical power, and Revelation 13 describes the wounded beast's recovery.

symbols.meaning: End-time atheistic and anti-biblical power, patterned after Egypt's defiance of the Lord.

wordNotes.explanation: At the time of the end, the king of the south pushes at the king of the north, and the king of the north responds like a whirlwind.
The king of the south, once literal Egypt, now carries the spiritual character of Egypt after the cross-centered transition of the prophecy.

notes.crossReferenceNotes: The final crisis includes both a shaking among professed believers and a gathering of sincere people out of confusion.

symbols.meaning: The visible Christian world entered by final papal influence and religious alliance.

wordNotes.explanation: The king enters the glorious land, many are overthrown, but Edom, Moab, and the chief of the children of Ammon escape out of his hand.
Edom, Moab, and Ammon were related to Israel yet often estranged from Israel.

symbols.meaning: The king stretches his hand upon the countries, and the land of Egypt does not escape. It marks a step in the prophetic sequence rather than introducing a separate coded symbol.

wordNotes.explanation: The king stretches his hand upon the countries, and the land of Egypt does not escape.
The king of the south remains spiritual Egypt in this end-time section, and the conflict broadens beyond one nation or region.

symbols.symbol: Prophetic phrase: treasures of gold and of silver
symbols.meaning: The king gains power over treasures of gold and silver and over the precious things of Egypt, while the Libyans and Ethiopians follow at his steps. It marks a step in the prophetic sequence rather than introducing a separate coded symbol.

wordNotes.term: treasures of gold and of silver
wordNotes.explanation: The king gains power over treasures of gold and silver and over the precious things of Egypt, while the Libyans and Ethiopians follow at his steps.
Libyans and Ethiopians were associated with the region and support of Egypt.

notes.crossReferenceNotes: The east and north point to the seal of God and the heavenly judgment message proclaimed in Revelation 14.

symbols.meaning: The sealing message of God that calls people to covenant loyalty.
The judgment-hour message from God's heavenly court and throne.

wordNotes.term: tidings out of the east and out of the north
wordNotes.explanation: Tidings from the east and from the north trouble the king, and he goes out with great fury to destroy many.
Just when the northern power appears successful, a message from God's direction interrupts it.

notes.crossReferenceNotes: Daniel 11 ends at the edge of the final crisis; Daniel 12 immediately answers with Michael standing and God's people delivered.

symbols.meaning: A final church-state union joining religious claims with royal power.
The peoples of the world on one side and God's faithful remnant on the other.

wordNotes.explanation: The king plants the tabernacles of his palace between the seas and the glorious holy mountain, yet he comes to his end and none helps him.
Planted between the sea and the glorious holy mountain, the image shows the final power standing between the peoples of the world and God's faithful remnant.
